newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed today in moderate trade amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slighty lower but bond prices were slightly higher. The interbank rate was unchanged from Tuesday," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.43/37 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.45/2.40 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.11/2.06 percent from 2.28/2.23 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.20/98.25 against Tuesday's close of S$97.95/98.00, September 2001 at S$98.20/98.25 versus S$97.73/97.78 and June 2003 at S$97.20/97.25 from S$96.73/96.78.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Tuesday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
